﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229DP
Exact geometric support split of K_cross by S and d; effective quadratic-height Sd physical fiber

1. Exact source and notation


Preserve the ORIGINAL physical Stage37 positive primitive four-square source P=(e,x,y,U,V,z,R) at R<=B with all selectors/chamber conditions, e²+x²=U², e²+y²=V², x²+y²=z², e²+x²+y²=R², and sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta), fixed 0<delta<1/3, G0=gcd(eR,xy). Retain current229DO moving auxiliary Z_B=B^(1/3)exp(-H Lambda), Lambda=logB/loglogB, H sufficiently large as fixed there; all old LOW costs charged once.


Use outer gaps A=R-U, Bv=R-V, C=R-z, S=A+Bv+C, R=S+2d and cone ABv+AC+BvC=2d², d>0, gcd(A,Bv,C)=1, exactly two gaps even. Let Omega=A Bv C, Pi=(A+Bv)(A+C)(Bv+C); K=Kcross=rad_odd(Omega Pi) is odd squarefree. Retain 229CC disjoint odd radical factors eta=rad_odd(gcd(A,Bv)gcd(A,C)gcd(Bv,C)), J=rad_odd(gcd(Omega,S)), tau, Ubar, Wbar, and K=eta*tau*J*Ubar*Wbar. All five are positive and pairwise coprime except Ubar/Wbar use separate 229CC stripped atoms; in particular eta,tau,J,Ubar,Wbar are pairwise coprime by229CC.


2. THEOREM 229DP.1 — exact FULL support intersection with physical S,d


For every primitive parity-compatible integer gap-cone triple, and thus every original full physical endpoint,
 gcd(K,d)=eta,                 (DP.1)
 gcd(K,S)=J,                   (DP.2)
 gcd(K,S*d)=eta*J,             (DP.3)
 gcd(S*d,K/(eta*J))=1,         (DP.4)
 K/(eta*J)=tau*Ubar*Wbar.     (DP.5)


All gcds are ordinary positive integer gcd; since K is odd squarefree no valuations or p=2 factors are being silently ignored.


Proof of DP.1, first direction: For any odd p|eta, p divides two gaps, say A,Bv; the cone modulo p gives 2d²==0, hence p|d. For the converse suppose odd p|d and p|K. If p|Omega, p divides at least one gap; say p|A. The cone then gives Bv*C==0 mod p, so p divides Bv or C and hence p|eta. If instead p|Pi, then p divides one sum; say p|A+Bv. Writing Bv==-A mod p in the cone gives -A²==2d²==0 mod p, so p divides A and Bv and again p|eta. The other colors are cyclic. This proves equality of odd prime supports and hence gcd(K,d)=eta.


Proof of DP.2: If odd p|J=rad_odd(gcd(Omega,S)), then p divides K and S. Conversely let odd p|K and p|S. If p|Omega, p divides a gap, say A, so p|Bv+C=S-A and hence p|J. If p|Pi, say p|A+Bv, then S=(A+Bv)+C implies p|C and thus p|Omega, so the preceding argument applies. Thus gcd(K,S)=J. Since eta and J are coprime by229CC, gcd(K,Sd)=rad(gcd(K,S)gcd(K,d))=eta J. Factoring the squarefree K proves DP.4-DP.5.


This exact theorem assigns the shared OUTER-GAP radical eta to the d-side and the OPPOSITE-INICIDENCE radical J to the S-side, and proves ALL residual odd cross-support tau Ubar Wbar is coprime to Sd. It is stronger than merely Q|d, J|S and gcd(gcd(S,d),K)=1. No density independence is asserted.


3. THEOREM 229DP.2 — effective fixed-value and fixed-rad(Sd) physical fibers


Define the positive physical scalar
 L_sd(P):=S*d,  with 0<L_sd<B²/2.                 (DP.6)
The height follows from S<R<=B and d=(R-S)/2<R/2.


Fix any n=L_sd(P). A pair (S,d) with positive S*d=n is determined by a divisor S|n and d=n/S, so has at most div(n) possibilities. With one pair fixed, the exact cone and coordinate reconstruction yield
 N_an=S²-6d²>0,
 Y=A+Bv-2C, X=A-Bv, and Y²+3X²=4N_an.       (DP.7)
Every integral (X,Y) of compatible parity corresponds to an Eisenstein algebraic integer alpha=(Y+X sqrt(-3))/2 of norm N_an. In Z[(1+sqrt(-3))/2], a UFD, there are at most 6 div(N_an) such alpha (retained229CW). Every (S,d,X,Y) fixes A,Bv,C exactly by
 C=(S-Y)/3,
 A=(2S+Y+3X)/6,
 Bv=(2S+Y-3X)/6.                            (DP.8)
Then 229BU reconstructs at most one positive original physical endpoint; square selectors and primitiveness only discard.
As n<B² and N_an<B², the quantitative229DO divisor bound gives, uniformly in n and B,
 #{P:R<=B, L_sd(P)=n} <= exp(C_1 Lambda).   (DP.9)


For a fixed radical r=rad(L_sd), L_sd<B² has prime support contained in r<=B². The effective prescribed-prime-support lemma229DO.1 with fixed A=C=2 yields at most exp(C_2 Lambda) possible L_sd integers. Combining with DP.9,
 #{P:R<=B, rad(Sd)=r} <= exp(C_3 Lambda),    (DP.10)
and uniformly for 1<=Z<=B,
 #{P:R<=B, rad(Sd)<=Z} <=(1+Z) exp(C_4 Lambda). (DP.11)
These are actual original-selector physical counts, not counts of arbitrary cone triples. The proof of the fiber is injective on the physical source. A finite arithmetic fixture is not used as population evidence.


4. NEW Stage37 high-K hardening at one synchronized cost


Let C_fib be the previous229DO effective finite low-auxiliary fiber constant. Choose H_prime sufficiently large to dominate both C_fib and C_4, for example H_prime=max(C_fib,C_4)+3. Set Z_prime=B^(1/3)exp(-H_prime Lambda). The earlier229DO low events and the NEW event rad(Sd)<=Z_prime have combined total count <=B^(1/3)exp(-Lambda) for sufficiently large B (a finite multiplicative constant is absorbed asymptotically).
The exact original S_B(delta) thus obeys
 #S_B(delta)
   <= B^(1/3)exp(-Lambda) + #H_B^DP(delta),           (DP.12)
where H_B^DP is the SAME full Stage37 physical source, all four exact squares/positive primitive/selectors/R<=B/sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta), with 229DO k13,N_an,rad7,outerrad3/numeric-pair hardness at Z_prime, and NEW rad(Sd)>Z_prime.
On H_B^DP, corrected229DJ O I³<=512K^9 and O,I>Z_prime³ give
 Kcross>0.5 B^(4/9)exp(-(4H_prime/3)Lambda),         (DP.13)
and exact DP.1-DP.5 give eta=gcd(K,d), J=gcd(K,S), and Kfree=K/(eta J)=tau Ubar Wbar coprime to S*d. These are simultaneous SAME-SOURCE conditions; the strengthened low-sector charge is one finite union, NOT independently multiplied sieve gains.


A single mixed SOURCE-MARKED value M(P)=G0(P)*S(P)*d(P) also has M<B^4/2 and fixed-M physical fibers <=exp(C Lambda) (choose Sd|M among div(M) choices and apply DP.9). Since G0>sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta) and rad(Sd)>Z_prime, on H_B^DP
 M > B^(2/3-delta)exp(-H_prime Lambda).                 (DP.14)
This is an OPTIONAL correlated B^4-height marked scalar, not a count of its large values.


5. Verification, firewall, and next research contract


A fresh independent finite exact integer fixture check of 1<=A,Bv,C<=150 with gcd(A,Bv,C)=1, exactly two even gaps, and integral d>0 with ABv+AC+BvC=2d² found 7587 cone-compatible fixtures. All 7587 passed gcd(K,d)=eta, gcd(K,S)=J, gcd(K,Sd)=eta J and eta,J coprime; 0 failures. The maximum observed SD fiber (within this bounded cone fixture box, not physical endpoints) was 30. These checks validate arithmetic only; the proof is prime-by-prime and the physical count derives from divisors/Eisenstein norms. No perfect-cuboid population estimate is inferred from fixtures.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229DO
Effective near-four-ninths Kcross exceptional-sector theorem via uniform divisor/smooth fibers


STATUS=NEW_EFFECTIVE_FREE_SCALE_ACTUAL_PHYSICAL_SCOPED_COUNT / 4_OVER_9_MINUS_O_1_ONE_HIGH_SUPPORT_RECEIVER / NO_GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT
CARD_DOC_ID=1rjxvy0YErsyV4ZYoBAz_Kko4msR1niL2TuwXUQh7Ojw

RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT
INDEPENDENT_HOSTILE_AUDIT_229DO=NOT_RUN


1. Exact physical source and purpose


Retain the SAME original positive primitive Stage37 physical four-square endpoint source S_B(delta), R<=B and all chamber/selector masks, with fixed 0<delta<1/3 and sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta), G0=gcd(eR,xy). Retain 229DN's free auxiliary cutoff independent of primary delta, 229CZ and229DG/229DH low-sector theorems, and corrected229DJ exact O I^3 identity. Unlike229DN, permit an auxiliary cutoff Z=Z(B) whose exponent approaches 1/3 instead of fixing a positive sigma. Such a moving cutoff is justified only after making the formerly unspecified B^o fiber losses quantitatively effective; this card supplies that justification.
Write b=log B and L=log log B (natural logarithms), assume B>=B0 large so L>1, and set Lambda=b/L. Every constant below depends only on the finite fixed Stage37 charts and their polynomial-height exponents, not on delta or B.


2. LEMMA 229DO.1 — explicit uniform polynomial-height divisor and smooth-support counts


For every FIXED A,C>0 there exist constants D(A),F(A,C)>0 such that for all sufficiently large B:
(a) max_{1<=n<=B^A} d(n) <= exp(D(A)*Lambda).
(b) For every integer m<=B^C,
 # {1<=n<=B^A : all prime divisors of n divide m}
     <=exp(F(A,C)*Lambda).
These are UNIFORM IN n AND m. The same holds for any fixed power d(n)^r, and for a fixed finite product of these bounds. It applies equally to an exact prescribed radical r, as that is a subset of m-smooth numbers with m=r.


Elementary proof without a PNT or advanced friable-number estimate. Split prime factors at Y=sqrt(b). Small primes p<=Y: there are at most Y of them; for an n<=B^A each exponent is <=Ab/log 2. Hence the number of possible small-prime exponent vectors is <=(1+Ab/log 2)^Y, with logarithm O_A(sqrt(b)*log b)=o(Lambda). Likewise their contribution to d(n) is <=this expression.
For large primes p>Y, log p> L/2. A fixed m<=B^C has at most 2Cb/L distinct large-prime divisors, while a permitted n<=B^A has total large-prime exponent sum <=2Ab/L. The nonnegative labelled exponent vectors with at most m0=floor(2Cb/L) positions and sum at most e0=floor(2Ab/L) number at most binomial(m0+e0,m0) <=2^(m0+e0)=exp(O_(A,C)(Lambda)); allowing fewer primes or n=1 only reduces the count. For d(n), using (e_p+1)<=2^e_p shows the large-prime factor is at most 2^(2Ab/L). Adding small-prime contributions proves both claims. In particular the formerly qualitative 229BQ support lemma admits the sharper effective uniform exp(O(Lambda)) form.


3. LEMMA 229DO.2 — effective synchronized low-auxiliary physical count


There exist absolute positive constants C_fib,C0,B0, depending only on the FIXED Stage37 fiber charts, such that for every B>=B0 and 1<=Z<=B,
  #{positive primitive full-four-square physical P:R<=B and at least one of the following LOW events}
  <= C0(1+Z)*exp(C_fib*Lambda).                         (DO.1)
LOW events are: k13<=Z (229BY+229BV/BT), N_an<=Z (229CW/229CX), any of the three numerical outer-gap pair products <=Z (229BL), any of the seven physical-coordinate radicals <=Z (229DG), any of the three outer-gap pair-product radicals <=Z (229DH/229BV). Original physical selector masks only remove candidates; the count is before primary sf(G0) restriction and thus remains valid after intersecting S_B(delta).


Proof audit by EXACT previous chart types, rather than an unquantified B^o substitution:
- 229BT/229DG seven fixed-coordinate fibers: bounded by fixed products of divisor counts d(a^2), d(z^2), or sum-of-two-squares representations <=4d(a^2), at polynomial B-height; Lemma229DO.1(a) makes each <=exp(C Lambda).
- 229BL numerical pair-gap low sector: fixed pair product n has at most fixed divisor-chart factorizations d(n)d(2n) by229BV, so summing n<=Z gives Z exp(C Lambda). This dominates the older O(Z^(1+o)).
- 229BV/229DH three outer-gap pair-radical fixed fibers: fixed product Q_e=A Bv or cyclic is counted by d(n)d(2n); the possible polynomial-height n supported on a fixed radical are counted by Lemma229DO.1(b), giving exp(C Lambda) per radical.
- 229BY pair-sum norm H_A=A²+2d² and cyclic: Z[sqrt(-2)] fixed-n representations <=O(d(n)^2), then factor st=n in <=d(n) ways; replacing n by fixed radical uses Lemma229DO.1(b). Thus k13's additional three radical events have exp(C Lambda) fibers. The k10 part is the preceding seven-coordinate/outer-pair receiver union.
- 229CW/229CX anisotropy N_an fixed-n physical fiber: real quadratic fixed-n ideal factorizations <=d(n)^r for one fixed r, O(1+log B) fixed fundamental-unit translates, and <=6d(n) Eisenstein norm representations; reconstruction is injective. These are <=exp(C Lambda) by Lemma229DO.1(a), because log(1+log B)=O(L)<<Lambda.
There are finitely many such events, and each fixed value/radical at most Z is summed at most Z times; one union bound gives (DO.1). All integer heights are <=B^M for FIXED M (at most a few), so C_fib is absolute and no hidden delta-dependent exponent remains. This is NOT an independence assumption.


4. THEOREM 229DO.3 — effective 4/9-o(1) physical low-K count


Choose the fixed sufficiently large constant
  H:=C_fib+2,
  Z_B := B^(1/3)*exp(-H*Lambda).                         (DO.2)
For all sufficiently large B, 1<Z_B<B and Lemma229DO.2 gives
  #LOW(Z_B) <= C0*(1+Z_B)*exp(C_fib*Lambda)
             <=B^(1/3)*exp(-Lambda).                       (DO.3)
All previous 229CZ,229DG,229DH hardening restrictions may therefore be imposed at this MOVING Z_B, with a genuine same-physical o(B^(1/3)) loss.


On their complement, 229DJ's CORRECTED exact (eta² included) identity
 O I^3 =512 Kcross^9/(J Ubar^7 Wbar^3)<=512 Kcross^9
and k13>Z_B plus rad(A Bv),rad(A C),rad(Bv C)>Z_B yield O,I>Z_B^3, hence
  Kcross >0.5 Z_B^(4/3)
         =0.5 B^(4/9)*exp(-(4H/3)*Lambda).          (DO.4)


For every original positive primitive full-four-square physical Stage37 source S_B(delta), with 0<delta<1/3 FIXED, the entire LOW-K population thus obeys
 # {P in S_B(delta): Kcross(P)
            <=0.5 B^(4/9)*exp(-(4H/3)*Lambda)}
       <=B^(1/3)*exp(-Lambda)
       =o(B^(1/3)).                                 (DO.5)
In exponent language the surviving radical support threshold is
  Kcross >0.5 B^(4/9-(4H/3)/loglog B).               (DO.6)
This improves the FIXED 229DN threshold Kcross>0.5B^(4/9-kappa) for every fixed kappa>0 once B is sufficiently large, while preserving the original primary delta. DO.5 is a NEW effective quantified low-support physical bound; the high-K endpoint count is NOT established.


5. Exact one-branch goal receiver and quantitative safeguards


Define H_B^eff(delta) as the actual full original S_B(delta) after all synchronized 229CZ/DG/DH high-auxiliary restrictions at the MOVING Z_B; Kcross condition DO.4 is DERIVED, not independently charged. Then
 #S_B(delta) <=B^(1/3)exp(-Lambda)+#H_B^eff(delta).  (DO.7)
Thus proving #H_B^eff(delta)=o(B^(1/3)) with ALL four square/positive primitive/original-selector/R-height conditions suffices for Stage37's unchanged one-third gate.
DO.5's error is smaller than B^(1/3) by exp(-logB/loglogB), NOT by a fixed negative power. No claim at the exact bare cutoff 0.5B^(4/9); no count of the large-K support image, no integer perfect cuboid existence/nonexistence, no P/M3 closure, no M3-T11-230.
The mechanism (fixed divisor/norm charts + synchronized pair-radical tests + corrected229DJ product) gives a near-4/9 necessary mark. Do NOT infer from it a density savings on HIGH-K, or substitute ambient cone solutions for exact physical endpoints. Do NOT multiply disjoint filters as if independent; one union bound on LOW is all that is used. All historical 229DI eta-free retractions stay in force. 229AR whole G0 parallel is unchanged.


6. Continuation / authority guard

For every odd prime p>3 and k>=1,
#S_k(p)=24*phi(p^k)=24(p^k-p^(k-1)) if p==1 or19 mod24, and #S_k(p)=0 for all other prime classes.
For admissible p, S_k is a DISJOINT union of 24 rank-one unit-parameter families: twelve with exactly one gap zero mod p^k and twelve with exactly one pair sum zero mod p^k. The reduction S_(k+1) -> S_k is surjective and every point of S_k has exactly p lifts within S_(k+1). The inverse limit contains 24 analytic Z_p-lines of primitive points; there is no additional exclusion by taking higher powers of the SAME three cone equations.


3. Exhaustive algebraic proof
Step 1. Reducing any primitive mod p^k solution mod p gives a nonzero F_p vector. Indeed if x=y=z=0 mod p, F=-2d² forces d=0 mod p (p>3), contradicting p-primitivity. Hence 229DE applies and p must be 1 or19 mod24; the residue is on one and ONLY one of the 24 projective lines.
Step 2 (unit-factor isolation). On every Omega-residue line, exactly one among the six factors x,y,z,x+y,x+z,y+z is zero mod p (namely the designated gap), while the other five are units. Therefore OmegaPi≡0 mod p^k FORCES that distinguished gap to equal 0 mod p^k. On every Pi-residue line, the distinguished pair sum alone is divisible by p, with all other five factors units; OmegaPi≡0 mod p^k forces the pair sum equal 0 mod p^k. This rules out split valuations among several factors.
Step 3 (Omega charts). After permutation put x=0 mod p^k, z=t a unit, y=r t, d=w t. Dividing F and N by t² gives
r²-r+1≡0 mod p^k, 2w²-r≡0 mod p^k.
Each of two mod-p r roots is simple: (2r-1)² = -3 mod p ≠0; each of two mod-p w roots is simple: 2w≠0 mod p. By elementary Hensel lifting, each ordered pair of roots extends uniquely to EVERY p^k. Each of three gap positions contributes 2*2=4 root pairs, thus 12 families, each with phi(p^k) choices of unit t.
Step 4 (Pi charts). After permutation put x=t a unit, y=-t, z=r t, d=w t. Dividing N,F by t² gives
r²+3≡0 mod p^k, 2w²+1≡0 mod p^k.
Each of the two r roots and the two w roots mod p is simple (p>3). Unique Hensel lifting gives 3 pair-sum positions *2*2=12 families, with phi(p^k) units each.
Step 5 (exhaustion, uniqueness). Different projective mod-p lines remain distinct upon lifting, and each primitive point has one designated zero factor. Every admissible pair has all required roots by 229DE; the explicit parametrizations satisfy the three equations. Thus 12+12=24 disjoint unit-parameter families, count 24 phi(p^k). On any fixed family, reduction of t mod p^(k+1) has p lifts; lifted root parameters are fixed uniquely by Hensel. Hence reduction fibers p, giving full p-adic saturation. No extra p-adic ray is missing.

The characters are constrained by the same equations and ARE NOT independent sieve factors. The 24 residue lines are smooth/unramified at odd p>3: all relevant one-variable root derivatives are p-units. This precludes a new obstruction from higher p powers WITHIN F=N=OmegaPi on the p-primitive cone.
The result does NOT assert all 24 p-adic lines lift to a GLOBAL Stage37 perfect-cuboid endpoint, or even to a point satisfying all four physical square equations, any real positivity, or selector constraints. Nor does it bound globally realized p, k, physical endpoint multiplicities, or occupied support. The prime p=3 is EXCLUDED and remains governed by 229DD physical 3|N_an iff3|J and v3(N_an)=1 under the 229CW q restriction. A local count of 24*phi(p^k) must NEVER be multiplied into a one-third global estimate without a genuine selector-aware distribution/large-sieve theorem.
Existing 229DD exact physical gcd(N_an,K_cross)=gcd(N_an,3*M24), 229DB weight13 hard13 six-bucket cover, 229CT J-primary and 229BZ retraction of 229BY Section5 remain untouched.


5. Arithmetic replay, independently reconstructing lifted roots
For p in 7,13,19,31,43,73,97 and k=1,2 (also p=19 k=3), an iterative root-lifting program computed every solution to the Omega chart polynomials r²-r+1=0, 2w²-r=0 and Pi chart polynomials r²+3=0, 2w²+1=0, then 3*(number of root-pairs) *phi(p^k). Outputs:
p=7,k=1/2:0/0;13:0/0;31:0/0.
p=19,k=1:432; k=2:8208; k=3:155952.
p=43,k=1:1008; k=2:43344.
p=73,k=1:1728; k=2:126144.

Each matches 24*phi(p^k). Additionally an independent exhaustive chart enumeration at modulus 19²=361 over all 361² normalized pairs (r,w) obtained exactly FOUR Omega and FOUR Pi pairs, the predicted numbers. N_an=x^2+y^2+z^2-xy-xz-yz=S^2-6d^2>0, K_cross=rad_odd(Omega Pi).

THEOREM 229DE.1 (exact local locus):
If p≠1,19 (mod24), there are NO nonzero vectors satisfying these three equations. If p≡1 or19 (mod24), the locus is the disjoint union of exactly 24 one-dimensional F_p-linear subspaces through the origin (24 distinct projective points), and has exactly 24(p-1) nonzero F_p-vectors. Twelve lines have exactly one gap zero (Omega case); twelve have exactly one pair sum zero (Pi case). No vector lies in both types for p>3.


2. Proof: Omega sector, twelve lines
Permute coordinates so x=0. A nonzero joint solution requires y,z≠0: if y=0, N_an=z^2=0 and F=-2d^2=0, hence the vector is zero because p>3.
Put z=t≠0, y=rt. From N_an=0 we get r^2-r+1=0 (r is a primitive sixth root of unity, requiring p≡1 mod3). From F=0 we get 2d^2=yz=r t^2, hence d=w t with w^2=r/2. Each admissible r has two w roots iff r/2 is a quadratic residue.
For p≡1 mod3, the quadratic character (r/p)=r^((p-1)/2)=(-1)^((p-1)/6), independent of the two sixth roots. Therefore (r/2|p)=(-1)^((p-1)/6)*(2/p). This equals +1 exactly for p≡1 or19 mod24, and -1 for p≡7 or13 mod24. There are exactly 2 choices of r, 2 of w, and 3 choices of zero gap: 12 disjoint lines {(0,rt,t,wt):t in F_p} with permutations. For p>3 the remaining pair sums are nonzero (otherwise N_an=3t²≠0), so these are not in the Pi sector.


3. Proof: Pi sector, twelve lines
Permute so x+y=0. Writing x=t≠0, y=-t, z=rt and d=w t, one obtains
N_an=(r²+3)t²=0, F=-(1+2w²)t²=0.
Thus r²=-3 and w²=-1/2. Existence requires (-3/p)=+1 and (-2/p)=+1, i.e. p≡1 or19 mod24 for p>3. There are exactly 2 choices of r, 2 of w, and 3 choices of the vanishing pair sum: another 12 disjoint lines {(t,-t,rt,wt):t in F_p} with permutations. None has a zero gap. The other two pair sums are nonzero since r≠±1 for p>3. If t=0 then N_an forces all three gaps and d zero, so no omitted nonzero solutions.


4. Exact geometry and counting firewall
The two 12-line sectors together prove the theorem; the only common vector between distinct lines is the excluded zero vector. In particular the 229DD residue restriction p≡1 or19 mod24 is sharp already on the primitive local cone. The local split characters (-3/p),(-2/p) arise from the SAME cone equations; (6/p)=+1 of 229DD follows from their product and is NOT an independent sieve saving.
This exact 24-point projective incidence classifies LOCAL residue witnesses, but is NOT a selector-aware count for physical endpoints. The positive primitive three-dimensional height source, unit/selector equations, and occupied-modulus distribution are not supplied by a finite-field locus count. Do NOT multiply 24/p² or other local density heuristics into the global one-third target, and do NOT claim the 24 classes all lift globally.
The 229DD exact physical gcd(N_an,K_cross)=gcd(N_an,3*M24), and 3|N_an iff3|J with v3(N_an)=1, stay unchanged. The 229DE theorem EXCLUDES p=3 and therefore does not replace 229DD's physical ramified-three analysis. The 229BZ retraction of 229BY Section5 remains binding.

Omega and Pi counts split equally at admissible p: p=19:216+216;43:504+504;73:864+864;97:1152+1152. In all nine tests there were zero Omega/Pi overlaps, and zero disagreements with the theorem. This tests local congruences only; verified perfect-cuboid endpoints are not produced.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229DD — anisotropy / union-radical 24-class obstruction and physical 3-adic equivalence


STATUS: POST_229DC_EXACT_24_CLASS_CROSS_SUPPORT / Q_DISJOINT_NORM6_SQUARE_ROOT / PHYSICAL_3_J_IFF_3_NAN / MOD9_RAMIFIED_FINGERPRINT / CONE_VS_PHYSICAL_SCOPE_AUDIT / NO_GLOBAL_COUNTING_GAIN / NO_REOPEN

1. Scope and exact current objects


Retain the exact positive primitive Stage37 physical endpoint source with R<=B, all face-squares/whole-diagonal/selector equations and masks, and primary sf(G0)>T0=B^(1/3-delta), 0<delta<1/3. The 229CZ/229DA/229DB two-scale HARD13 auxiliary Z=B^(1/3-delta/2) remains valid with k13>Z, N_an>Z and all three 229BL pair-products>Z, at o(B^(1/3)) cost. K_cross>Z is implied by k13>Z, not a 14th independent hard restriction.


Use A=R-U, Bv=R-V, C=R-z, S=A+Bv+C=R-2d, ABv+AC+BvC=2d², Omega=A Bv C, Pi=(A+Bv)(A+C)(Bv+C),
  N_an=S²-6d²=A²+Bv²+C²-ABv-AC-BvC>0,
  K_cross=rad_odd(Omega Pi)=eta*tau*J*M_U*M_V*M_z.


The retained 229CW result supplies q=gcd(S,d)=gcd(R,S)=gcd(R,d), with every prime p|q satisfying p==1 mod12, and gcd(q,Omega Pi)=1; the latter suffices for the cross-support proof. 229DC already established gcd(N_an,eta*tau)=1 and all shared odd primes >3 between N_an and K_cross are p==1 mod3 in one matched M_i, with J overlap possible only at 3.


2. NEW quadratic-norm splitting obstruction at the shared primes


Suppose an odd prime p>3 divides both N_an and K_cross.


Because p|K_cross, p|Omega Pi, while gcd(q,Omega Pi)=1. If p|d, the norm equation S²-6d²==0 mod p forces p|S, so p|gcd(S,d)=q, contradiction. Thus
  p does not divide d.                                    (DD.1)


Reducing N_an=S²-6d² modulo p and dividing by the unit d² gives
  (S d^{-1})² == 6 mod p.                                  (DD.2)


Therefore (6/p)=+1. Independently 229DC proved p==1 mod3. Quadratic reciprocity gives, for p>3,
  p==1 mod3 and (6/p)=1
    iff p==1 or 19 mod24.                                 (DD.3)


Further 229DC localizes such a prime to M_U*M_V*M_z, not eta,tau or J. Hence every p>3 dividing gcd(N_an,K_cross) is a matched-M prime congruent to 1 or 19 modulo 24.


RESULT_229DD_NAN_KCROSS_SHARED_PRIMES_24_CLASS_ONLY=PROVED_EXACT.
This sharpens 229DC's p==1 mod3 into a genuine quadratic-character intersection. In particular matched M_i primes in residue classes 7 or 13 mod24 CANNOT divide N_an, even though they split in Q(sqrt(-3)). The argument uses the actual coupled norm and the same q support once, not independent sieve factors.


3. NEW physical-only complete ramified-three equivalence


The following strengthened 3-adic conclusion requires the retained PHYSICAL 229CW theorem that 3 cannot divide q. It is NOT claimed for every ambient primitive cone fixture.


Since N_an=S²-6d²,
  3|N_an iff 3|S.                                         (DD.4)
If 3|S, then 3 does not divide d, because 3 does not divide q=gcd(S,d) on the exact physical source.


The cone identity gives
  A²+Bv²+C²=S²-4d²== -d²==2 mod3.
A square modulo3 is 0 or1, so exactly TWO of A,Bv,C are nonzero modulo3 and the remaining ONE gap is divisible by3. Thus 3|Omega and 3|S, hence 3|J=rad_odd(gcd(Omega,S)).


Conversely 3|J directly implies 3|S and hence 3|N_an. Therefore on the exact Stage37 PHYSICAL source:
  3|N_an iff 3|S iff 3|J.                                (DD.5)


Because 3|S and 3∤d in this case,
  N_an=S²-6d²==3 mod9,
  v_3(N_an)=1.                                            (DD.6)


In particular, on the physical source 3|N_an implies 3|K_cross (through J), and the ramified-three contribution to the common support is exactly gcd(3,N_an)=gcd(3,J).


RESULT_229DD_PHYSICAL_NAN_THREE_IFF_J_THREE=PROVED_EXACT_WITH_RETAINED_229CW_Q_THEOREM.
RESULT_229DD_PHYSICAL_NAN_THREE_HAS_V3_EXACTLY_ONE=PROVED_EXACT.


SCOPE CORRECTION to the 229DC caveat:
229DC stated that 3 may divide N_an without 3 dividing J, a statement valid for the BROADER primitive cone but unnecessary and overly cautious if read as a statement about the retained full PHYSICAL source. It is now excluded on actual physical endpoints by 229CW's q support theorem. Do NOT erase the genuine cone counterfixtures.


Concrete cone-only counterfixture:
  (A,Bv,C,d)=(1,10,40,15),
  S=51, ABv+AC+BvC=450=2*15²,
  gcd(A,Bv,C)=1, exactly two gaps even,
  N_an=S²-6d²=1251=9*139,
  J=rad(gcd(400,51))=1,
  q=gcd(S,d)=3.
This satisfies the primitive parity cone but violates 229CW physical q prime-support (3 cannot divide q), so it cannot challenge (DD.5). It also demonstrates why the q input must be explicitly retained in the equivalence.


4. Exact support-filtered full intersection


Define M_24 as the squarefree product of exactly those primes dividing M_U*M_V*M_z and congruent to 1 or19 modulo24. Because the three M_i are pairwise coprime odd squarefree, M_24 is unambiguous and 3∤M_24.


The retained 229DC gcd formula, the new (DD.3), and physical (DD.5) combine to
  gcd(N_an,K_cross)
     = gcd(N_an,M_24)*gcd(3,J)
     = gcd(N_an,M_24)*gcd(3,N_an)
     = gcd(N_an,3*M_24).                                  (DD.7)


This is an exact cross-support identity on FULL PHYSICAL Stage37 endpoints, not a probabilistic independence or an occupied-value count.


RESULT_229DD_EXACT_24_FILTERED_NAN_KCROSS_GCD=PROVED_EXACT_ON_PHYSICAL_SOURCE.


5. Verifications and quantitative firewall


A finite cone replay over all 2433 labelled primitive positive parity-compatible A,Bv,C<=85 with integral positive d satisfying ABv+AC+BvC=2d² checked ALL 1146 distinct incidences (fixture, shared odd prime p) with p|gcd(N_an,rad_odd(Omega Pi)). For p>3 all were p==1 or19 mod24; no failures. Incidences by residue: p=3, 936; p==19 mod24, 198; p==1 mod24, 12.


Among these cone fixtures, 1080 had 3|N_an; 144 had 3|N_an but 3∤J, all arising outside the full physical theorem's allowable 3∤q condition. This confirms the scope boundary is material, not cosmetic.


Additional direct modular checks of ALL nonzero (e,x,y) modulo p and all possible roots U,V,z,R satisfying all four physical square equations yielded:
  p=3: 48 modular tuples, 0 with q==0 mod3 or 3|N_an but 3∤J;
  p=7: 720 tuples, 0 N_an-K_cross overlaps;
  p=13: 3648 tuples, 0 overlaps;
  p=19: 7344 tuples, 1296 N_an-K_cross overlaps;
  p=31: 38160 tuples, 0 overlaps;
  p=37: 52416 tuples, 0 overlaps.
